entries.clue: Hack down willow without determination, mate (6)

blocks.note: to fell a tree is to hack it down

annotation.surface: A lumberjack chops down a willow half-heartedly and calls to a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' reads as a word shouted at the end of the sentence, but it is the definition: a fellow is a companion.
annotation.definitionFit: A fellow is a companion or comrade, which is what a mate is.

entries.clue: Use gun then use fists in really hot spot (7)

blocks.note: to fire a gun
to box is to fight with fists

annotation.surface: A violent sequence of shooting then brawling in a dangerous place.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'hot spot' sounds like a trouble zone, but here it is literal: the firebox is where a boiler or locomotive burns its fuel. The answer also hides two trees, FIR and BOX, which 10 across needs.
annotation.definitionFit: A firebox is the chamber of a furnace or steam engine where the fire burns, so it is literally a very hot spot.

entries.clue: Cut cedar, initially in way (5)

first letter of cedar, placed inside LANE

annotation.surface: An instruction to cut down a cedar that stands in the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a command about the cedar; it is the definition, as in lancing a boil.
annotation.definitionFit: To lance is to cut open with a sharp blade, as a surgeon does.

entries.clue: American word for elder in Arnold’s terminology (7)

annotation.definitionFit: Oldster is an informal, chiefly American word for an older person.

entries.clue: Black part of forest, comparatively leafless (6)

annotation.surface: A dark patch of woodland that has lost more leaves than the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Comparatively' signals a comparative adjective; balder, like a tree with fewer leaves, fits.
annotation.definitionFit: Bald can mean bare of covering, so balder is more bare, comparatively leafless.

entries.clue: Italian tree’s interior destroyed, not in isolation (5,4)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' hints at a Latin phrase, which the answer is, though the country only supplies the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for 'among other things', so what it describes is not alone.

entries.clue: Isn’t comfortable around gum trees right away concealing article (7)

the definite article, placed inside TEES

annotation.surface: Someone uneasy near eucalyptus trees, which Australians call gum trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gum trees' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between them: 'gum' belongs to the definition, the sore mouth of a baby cutting teeth.
annotation.definitionFit: A teething baby is uncomfortable in the gums while its teeth come through.

entries.clue: Eucalyptus, say, he put out with plant put stop to everything (3,2,3,5)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks botanical beside the eucalyptus, but it means an industrial plant.

entries.clue: Great architect, builder of treehouse (4)

the bird builds its nest in trees

annotation.surface: Praise for a famous architect who also built a treehouse.
annotation.walkthrough: A treehouse sounds like a child's den; a bird's nest is a house in a tree, and the wren builds one.
annotation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren designed St Paul's; the wren is a small bird that nests in trees.

entries.clue: Part of horsedrawn vehicle left when European departs 1d or 19 (10)

annotation.walkthrough: E is the abbreviation for European. Take it from FIREBOX (1 down) or EYEWASH (19 down) and each leaves a pair of trees, literally a double tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A doubletree is the crossbar on a carriage that lets two horses pull side by side.

annotation.definitionFit: Your next of kin are your closest relatives, those nearest you on the family tree.

entries.clue: Small feller’s tool, kind of blue (4)

entries.clue: Place such as 25 where bark may be secured (7)

annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Deal on the Kent coast is a port town where ships tie up.

entries.clue: It helps one clearly see nonsense (7)
